description: Revisions of the extrinsic hand muscles from the hand rebuild: the juncturae tendinum between EDC3, EDC4 and EDC5 (junction nodes on the tendons and tension-only links), the flexor carpi ulnaris over the pisiform and the hamate hook, the force of FDS5, the side sites of the forearm wraps (outside their geoms), APL at the thumb CMC after Barry et al. 2018, and the extensor carpi ulnaris through the groove of the ulnar head. Written into the right-arm XML by scripts/generate_extrinsic_muscles.py (--fit refits the junctura stiffness and the FCU pisiform and ECU groove sites; --fit-ecu only the ECU site).

juncturae.method: Junctura tendinum links between the extensor digitorum tendons of the ring and the middle finger (EDC4-EDC3) and of the ring and the little finger (EDC4-EDC5); the index-middle link is omitted (2nd interspace: 63 % prevalence, 95 % thin type 1, Yammine 2015; von Schroeder & Botte 1993 find the radial coupling carried by the intertendinous fascia and the web). Each tendon carries a junction node: a light body on a slide joint in its metacarpal, on the EDC path segment from the metacarpal via site to the MCP wrap, tied by a tendon equality to the tendon's branched path from its via point proximal of the node (EDC-P4, so the helper takes the tendon's MCP wrap and the node moves with the tendon material; the S6 lumbrical-node primitive and settings). The links run from the ring tendon's node obliquely distally to the neighbours' nodes (the juncturae arise from the ring tendon and insert more distally on the neighbours) as tension-only spatial tendons, taut from the longer of their lengths with straight fingers and in the relaxed resting posture. Stiffness fitted to von Schroeder & Botte 1993's junctura share of the neighbour MP extension under 1.5 kg traction (intact minus juncturae cut).

fit.protocol: myohand_r, wrist and forearm held at 0, thumb held, gravity 9.81 m/s2 toward the palm (palm down), no excitation; settle 2 s from the resting posture of von Schroeder & Botte (MP 56, PIP 35, DIP 17 deg), then 14.7 N (1.5 kg) on one EDC tendon (applied along its path), 1.5 s; net MP extension of the neighbours with the links minus without them (the model has no web or fascia coupling).

EDC4_traction.where: pp. 644-645, Fig. 5: MP-long 38 -> 20 deg and MP-small 44 -> 22 deg after cutting the juncturae and fascia

EDC3_traction.where: p. 645, Fig. 4: MP-ring 26 -> 18 deg, MP-small 16 -> 9 deg

fit.weights_note: No SDs are printed for these differences; equal weights in deg.
fit.own_finger_note: mcp4 under EDC4 traction and mcp3 under EDC3 traction: target 0 deg change from the links (the pulled finger's own extension is the same with and without the juncturae: traction on one tendon or on all gave the same result, p. 643)

stiffness_bounds_N_per_m.method: upper bound numerical: a tendon spring is explicit in MuJoCo's Euler step. With EDC4 and the middle-finger flexors fully active the JT34 force changes step to step by 0.17 N at 1e3 N/m (5.5 N mean), 0.59 N at 3e3 and 3.5 N at 1e4 N/m (38 N mean); node armature does not help. The transfer saturates (the link's obliquity limits it): under EDC4 traction the middle-finger MP extends 31.5 deg at 1e3 N/m and 32.9 deg at 1e4 N/m. Both are far below the softest extensor-hood segments of Garcia-Elias et al. 1991b (40 N/mm), so the links are softer than the tissue

fcu.method: FCU runs over the pisiform (a sesamoid in its tendon) and on along the pisohamate ligament past the hamate hook to the base of MC5 (pisometacarpal ligament), so it crosses CMC5. The pisiform via point is fitted within the pisiform's bounding box (the tendon on the bone's palmar surface) to Horii 1993's neutral moment arms; the hamate-hook via point is the hamate mesh vertex nearest the pisiform. The split of the force between the pisohamate and pisometacarpal ligaments is not modelled (one line to the MC5 base). The path proximal of the pisiform stays on the radius, so the moment arms do not change with forearm rotation (Horii 1993: no significant change).
fcu.lengthrange_note: MoBL lengthrange and FCU length at q0 before the re-route (S6 model); the lengthrange is shifted by the length change at q0

fit.bounds: pisiform mesh bounding box in its body frame

fds5.method: MyoHand's extrinsic forces are Holzbaur et al. 2005's peak forces scaled by muscle-specific factors (FDS2-4: 2.66, 2.84, 2.96 x). FDS5 was 4.56 x (75.3 N against 16.5 N), out of line with its group and with Lieber 1992's small FDS5 (PCSA 0.40 cm2, a quarter of FDS4). Its force is set to Holzbaur's 16.5 N times the mean FDS2-4 factor. Its optimal fibre length is already Lieber's 42 mm renormalised to a 2.7 um sarcomere (Holzbaur's 5.2 cm; model 51.5 mm) and is kept; FDS2's 83.5 mm equals Lieber's combined bellies (68 mm) renormalised, while Matsuzawa 2021's 32.9 mm is a single belly.

thumb_extrinsics.method: APL crosses the thumb CMC on Barry et al. 2018's routing (their path points in MyoHand's identical bone frames); the forearm and wrist part of the path is unchanged: from the forearm over a via site on the trapezium to Barry's insertion on the MC1 base (APL-P7_r, moved; APL-P8_r removed). Moment arms against Smutz et al. 1998 at their neutral (mid-point of the CMC ranges, MP 0).

APL-P7_r.note: Barry's APL insertion on the MC1 base (was a via point before APL-P8_r)

not_adopted.FPL: Barry's FPL CMC routing (trapezium point and first MC1 point) raises FPL's CMC flexion arm at Smutz's neutral from 4.2 to 14.3 mm (Smutz 14.3 +- 4.0; RMS z 2.50 -> 1.70), but the lateral pinch then has no solution within its off-axis limit (best 3.6 N at 14x the limit); the trapezium point alone (13.8 mm) gives the same. Not adopted.

radius_m.method: the ellipsoid's larger cross-section semi-axis; 3.5-8 mm give the same arms within 0.6 mm

side_angle_deg.method: middle of the band of side directions (180-270 deg from the cylinder's x axis) over which the tendon wraps the cylinder at every Smutz posture; outside the cylinder

apl_via.method: The cylinder gave a 44 mm snap under MuJoCo 4 and took APL around its far side. A via site on the trapezium replaces it and via point APL-P6_r, fitted to Smutz et al. 1998's arms at their neutral with APL an abductor over the CMC range (build/data/side_sites.json, vias).

wrap_sides.method: Each wrist (and PQ's ulnar) wrap whose side site sat inside its geom (the inside wrap, which MuJoCo and mujoco-warp solve differently where the deflection is small) gets its side site outside the geom, distance_radii radii from the centre along direction_body, on the side where the tendon runs: dorsal (+z of lunate_r) for the extensors, palmar for FCR and PQ. Where the arm curves then jump or leave Horii 1993's bands, the geom's centre and radius are refitted (bounded) to Horii's neutral arms and the arm curves of the inside wrap. ECRL keeps its inside wrap: with its side site outside, no sphere within 8 mm of its place and 1/3-3 times its radius keeps ECRL an extensor beyond 45 deg wrist extension (open). ECU belongs to the forearm-rotation revision; the shoulder wraps are a later step.

PQ.method: palmar of the ulna (the PQ wraps the ulna's palmar surface in pronation); geometry unchanged

wrap_sides.replaced: FCR, ECRB, EDM: their small spheres or wide cylinder gave length jumps; each is now a via site on the lunate (build/data/side_sites.json, vias).

ecu.method: ECU runs in the groove on the dorsal (posterior) surface of the ulnar head, radial to the styloid, held there by its own subsheath, which is fixed to the ulna and does not turn with the radius (Horii 1993: the ECU alone among the wrist motors changes its moment arms with forearm rotation). Its via point ECU-P5_r moves from the radius to the ulna, at the distal end of the groove; distal of it the tendon runs straight to the MC5 base (ECU-P6_r). The site is fitted within the groove's surface: on the posterior to lateral side of the ulnar head, 0.5 to 3 mm outside the sphere fitted to the head's mesh vertices (the tendon lies in the groove, below the head's outline), to the extension and ulnar-deviation moment arms of Horii 1993 and Loren 1996 in supination, neutral and pronation. The wrap sphere on the radius (ECU_torus_wrap_r, its side site at the sphere's centre) and its unused duplicates (ECU_torus_r, ECU_sidesite_r) are removed: with the groove on the ulna the tendon never reaches a sphere there. The path proximal of the groove is unchanged (sites on the humerus and the ulna); the forearm rotation axis is unchanged (it already passes through the radial and ulnar heads; axis_check).
ecu.rotations_note: pro_sup_r: -90 = supination, +90 = pronation; wrist neutral, elbow as in q0. Neither source gives the angles of its supinated and pronated positions.

ulnar_head.method: least-squares sphere through the ulna mesh vertices within 22 mm of the distal end of the ulna (the head)

radial_head.method: least-squares circle, in the plane normal to the rotation axis, through the radius mesh vertices within 7 mm of its proximal end (the head)

bounds.method: spherical coordinates about the fitted head centre: angle around the rotation axis from posterior (dorsal) toward lateral (radial), up to the edge of the radioulnar joint; angle from the proximal axis direction (> 90 deg = distal half of the head); distance outside the fitted sphere

mcp_pulleys.method: The extrinsic finger tendons cross the MCP on cylinders on the joint's flexion axis (in the metacarpal), with the side site two radii out on the palmar (flexors) or dorsal (extensors) side. Before, FDS and FDP 2-5 (except FDP2, which keeps its wrap) crossed the MCP on via sites only: their arm fell from 6-10 mm at 0 deg to 0-2 mm at -60 deg (FDS3 turned extensor), and EDC2 and EDC3 turned flexor past about -45 deg because the PP hood site passed their via site on the metacarpal head. Flexors: Landsmeer's model III in flexion from the via sites (arm rises with flexion, as An et al. 1983 Fig. 4 and Brook et al. 1995), the cylinder holds the 0 deg arm in hyperextension (the tendons lie on the palmar plate); its radius is the path's own arm at 0 deg, so flexion is unchanged. Extensors: Landsmeer's model I (constant arm, Brook et al. 1995; An et al. 1983 Fig. 4), radius from An et al. 1983 (index) scaled by An et al. 1979 for digits 3-5; the via site before the hood moves to 135 deg from distal on the metacarpal neck, 1 mm outside the cylinder, so the hood site no longer passes it; past about -30 deg the tendon leaves the cylinder and its arm rises a little (bowstring). No measured MCP moment arm in hyperextension was found.

mcp_pulleys.side_note: Side sites two radii out at side_deg about the MCP axis (0 = distal, 90 = dorsal), in the metacarpal. Flexors: -90 (palmar). Extensors: 105, near the middle of the short dorsal arc in slight hyperextension, where it is shortest: at 90 deg MuJoCo 3's nearest-arc rule took the long palmar arc near -15 deg (and a side site on the proximal phalanx jumped on MuJoCo 3 with the MCP abducted). The ray opposite the site (-75 deg) is reached by the hood sites only past about 108 deg of flexion, beyond the limit and its 7.5 deg sampling margin, so the paths are continuous on MuJoCo 4 and 3.17 over -68..97 deg at every abduction.

pip_pulleys.method: FDS2-4 and FDP2-5 cross the PIP on a cylinder on the joint's flexion axis (in the proximal phalanx), inserted after the last site of the proximal phalanx, with the side site two radii out on the palmar side. Before, they crossed the PIP on via sites only: past about 60-80 deg the middle-phalanx site came close to the joint and the segment from the proximal-phalanx site swung over it, so the flexion arm fell (FDS2 and FDS3 turned extensor past about 100-105 deg, FDP2 went from +10.4 to -10.4 mm between 90 and 110 deg, FDP4 and FDP5 fell to under 1 mm at 115 deg). The cylinder holds the arm in deep flexion, where the tendons lie on the palmar plate and in the A3 pulley; its radius is the path's own arm at 0 deg, rounded down to 0.1 mm, so the arms from 0 deg up to the via-site peak do not change. FDS5 keeps its via sites (2.8-10.2 mm over the range, no fall). Literature: flexor PIP arms rise with flexion (Landsmeer's model III; An et al. 1979 Fig. 12; Brook et al. 1995) and average 7.9 (FDP) and 6.2 mm (FDS) over 0-90 deg for the index (An et al. 1983); no measured arm beyond about 90 deg was found.
